q: Under SA 520, a substantive analytical procedure differs from an analytical procedure used in risk assessment principally because the substantive procedure:
o: Must be carried out at the planning stage of every audit engagement
Must be documented in full within the overall audit strategy memorandum
Must be applied only to income statement balances and never to balance sheet items
Requires an expectation precise enough to detect a material misstatement
why: A substantive analytical procedure only gives assurance if the expectation is precise enough to detect a material misstatement. Risk assessment analytics may be broad and imprecise since their purpose is to identify areas of risk, not to obtain substantive evidence.

q: Which situation makes a substantive analytical procedure MOST likely to be effective on its own?
o: A high volume of predictable items such as rent from long fixed leases
A small number of complex construction contracts carrying variable claims
Provisions for litigation determined largely by management judgement
Related party transactions occurring at irregular and uneven intervals
why: Analytical procedures work best where relationships are stable, predictable, and driven by known factors such as fixed rents and known occupancy. Judgemental, low volume, or irregular balances lack the predictability needed to build a precise expectation.

q: An auditor develops an expectation for payroll cost using headcount times average salary and finds a difference of 4 percent from the recorded amount. The threshold for investigation should be set:
o: At performance materiality, since anything smaller than that is immaterial
By reference to the difference acceptable without further investigation
At the level of the largest individual payroll variance seen during the year
At 5 percent, which is the accepted rule of thumb for payroll analytics
why: SA 520 requires the auditor to determine an acceptable difference by reference to materiality and the assurance sought, not a fixed rule. Setting the threshold at full performance materiality would leave no allowance for aggregation with other misstatements.

q: Which factor most directly improves the PRECISION of a substantive analytical procedure over revenue?
o: Using annual totals for the whole year rather than monthly or weekly data
Using unaudited budgets prepared by management as the expectation
Building the expectation from revenue disaggregated by product and site
Comparing current year revenue only with prior year revenue in total
why: Disaggregation reduces the chance that offsetting movements hide a misstatement, so it sharply improves precision. Annual totals and simple prior year comparisons are the least precise, and unaudited budgets carry management bias unless their reliability is tested.

q: The auditor uses data produced by the entity system as an input to a substantive analytical procedure. SA 520 requires the auditor to:
o: Accept the data where general IT controls were tested in a prior year
Use the data only after the internal audit function has fully reviewed it
Obtain a written representation from management that the data is accurate
Evaluate data reliability by testing controls over it or the data itself
why: Reliability of the underlying data is a precondition for any assurance from the analytical procedure, and it must be established by testing controls or the data itself. A written representation is not a substitute for evidence, and prior year control testing does not carry forward automatically.

q: A gross margin analysis shows margin has been stable at 32 percent for three years despite a documented 12 percent increase in input costs and no price increase. The auditor should conclude that:
o: The absence of an expected fluctuation is itself a matter to investigate
The stability confirms firm cost control, so no further work is needed
The procedure has failed and every purchase must now be tested in detail
The margin should be recomputed using net rather than gross sales figures
why: SA 520 treats relationships that fail to fluctuate as expected in the same way as unexpected fluctuations, both signalling possible misstatement. Reading stability as automatically favourable is the classic error, as it can indicate manipulation of inventory or cost of sales.

q: When an analytical procedure identifies a fluctuation inconsistent with other information, the auditor should FIRST:
o: Propose an audit adjustment for the full amount of the difference found
Accept the management explanation where it is plausible for the business
Inquire of management and corroborate the responses with other evidence
Report the difference to those charged with governance as a deficiency
why: SA 520 requires inquiry of management followed by corroboration of the responses with other audit evidence. Accepting a plausible explanation without corroboration is precisely what the standard prohibits, because plausibility alone is not evidence.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of a plausible and predictable relationship suitable for substantive analytics?
o: Advertising spend in one year against the revenue of the following year
Employee numbers and pay scales against payroll for a stable staff
Directors remuneration measured against the reported profit before tax
Legal provision balances measured against the growth rate of revenue
why: Payroll driven by known headcount and pay rates is a strong and stable relationship with verifiable inputs. Advertising to revenue, remuneration to profit, and provisions to revenue are all weak or judgement driven relationships with poor predictive power.

q: For which assertion is a substantive analytical procedure over interest expense on a term loan MOST persuasive?
o: Completeness and accuracy, given known principal, rate and schedule
Rights and obligations attaching to the underlying bank borrowing itself
Existence of the lending institution as a separate legal entity
Classification of the loan between current and non-current portions
why: Recomputing expected interest from principal, rate, and tenure is a strong test of whether the recorded charge is complete and accurate. Rights, existence of counterparties, and current versus non-current split need documentary examination rather than analytics.

q: An auditor plans to rely solely on substantive analytical procedures for a material revenue stream assessed as having a significant risk. Under the standards this is:
o: Acceptable, provided the expectation developed is sufficiently precise
Acceptable, provided management gives a signed representation on revenue
Acceptable only where the internal audit function has tested that stream
Not acceptable, since a significant risk demands tests of details
why: Where a significant risk is identified, substantive procedures responsive to that risk must include tests of details, so analytics alone are insufficient. Precision of the expectation does not remove that requirement.

q: The MOST important reason an auditor disaggregates data by month when performing analytics over cost of sales is that:
o: Monthly data is inherently more reliable than annual summary data
Offsetting misstatements between periods are less likely to be hidden
It removes the need to test the reliability of the underlying source data
Monthly data automatically satisfies the requirement for tests of details
why: Annual aggregation lets overstatements in one period offset understatements in another, so monthly analysis narrows the window in which errors can hide. Disaggregation does not make data inherently more reliable, and reliability testing is still required.

q: Which of the following would MOST undermine the effectiveness of a trend analysis of repairs and maintenance expense?
o: A stable manufacturing base with no change in capacity during the year
Consistent vendor and annual maintenance contract arrangements year on year
A material change in the capitalisation policy during the current year
Repairs expense standing at 3 percent of revenue in both of the years
why: A change in the capitalisation threshold breaks the comparability of the trend, because amounts previously expensed may now sit in fixed assets. The other options describe conditions of stability, which make trend analysis more, not less, effective.

q: SA 520 requires analytical procedures to be performed near the end of the audit in order to:
o: Replace the need for a final review of the statements by the partner
Confirm that every journal entry posted in the year has been tested
Recalculate the materiality level to be used for the following year
Help form an overall conclusion that the statements are consistent
why: Closing analytics support the overall conclusion by testing whether the statements as a whole align with the auditor understanding of the entity. They are additional to, not a substitute for, the partner review and other required procedures.

q: An auditor computes expected depreciation as opening gross block times the average rate and finds a difference of 9 percent. The MOST likely legitimate cause to investigate first is:
o: A change in useful life estimates or major additions and disposals
A misstatement in the trade payables balance at the reporting date
An error in the cut-off applied to revenue around the year end
An understatement of the deferred tax liability carried in the accounts
why: A simple opening balance model ignores mid year additions, disposals, and revisions to useful lives, all of which shift the depreciation charge. The other items sit in unrelated cycles and would not explain a depreciation variance.

q: When using industry data as the basis for an expectation, the principal limitation is that:
o: Industry composite data is never made publicly available in India at all
Industry data may not be used for risk assessment purposes at all
Policies, product mix and scale may differ from the industry composite
Using industry data converts the procedure into a test of controls
why: Composite industry figures blend entities with different policies, mixes, and scale, so differences may reflect these rather than misstatement. That limits precision but does not bar the data from being used as a risk assessment input.

q: The auditor sets the acceptable difference for a substantive analytical procedure over rental income at 25 percent of performance materiality rather than 100 percent. This choice reflects:
o: A wish to reduce the overall audit effort spent on rental income
A need for higher assurance and room to aggregate other misstatements
A requirement of SA 320 that every threshold be a quarter of materiality
An assessment that the risk of material misstatement here is very low
why: A tighter threshold is set when more assurance is being drawn from the procedure and to leave room for aggregating undetected misstatements elsewhere. A tighter threshold increases rather than reduces audit effort, and no standard prescribes a fixed fraction.

q: Which is a valid reason to perform an analytical procedure as a risk assessment procedure even though it will provide no substantive assurance?
o: It may flag unusual transactions, amounts or ratios indicating risks
It satisfies the need for sufficient appropriate evidence over balances
It automatically reduces the sample size required for tests of details
It allows the auditor to omit the understanding of internal control
why: Risk assessment analytics are required precisely to flag unusual items and relationships that point to risks needing response. They do not themselves constitute substantive evidence, nor do they displace the required understanding of internal control.

q: An entity records a 30 percent revenue rise while receivables days increase from 45 to 96 and operating cash flow declines. The MOST appropriate auditor response is to:
o: Accept the movement as normal for a company in a growth phase
Rely on the management representation that all recorded revenue is genuine
Increase materiality to reflect the larger revenue base for the year
Treat it as an indicator of overstatement and design specific procedures
why: Revenue growing far faster than cash collection is a classic fraud and cut-off indicator that calls for targeted procedures on occurrence and recoverability. Raising materiality or relying on a representation would reduce rather than increase the response to a heightened risk.
